faq.q: How does Aperture differ from traditional bundlers like Vite or Webpack?
faq.a: Aperture focuses exclusively on generating self-contained, immutable static documents with physical tactile aesthetics. It injects zero JavaScript framework runtimes, compiling semantics, layout, and static textures directly into a single HTML file.

faq.q: Can files compiled with Aperture be viewed completely offline?
faq.a: Yes. All fonts, textures, and stylesheets utilize local relative paths or Base64 embeddings. The resulting standalone HTML files can be opened directly from local drives and will render accurately decades later.

faq.q: How can I integrate Aperture into existing CI/CD automation pipelines?
faq.a: Aperture provides a standard CLI and Node.js API. A single command, aperture compile, handles validation and compilation, returning standard exit codes (0/1) for seamless CI integration.
